In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ODC activity in normal mucosa of the colon is higher in cases of multiple adenocarcinomas and/or adenomas than in cases of a single adenocarcinomata.
ODC is an enzyme that may be useful in the early detection of cancer, and that its activity may provide a good marker to identify individuals at higher risk.
ODC is increased in large bowel with tumors, adenocarinomas, and adenomas and is higher in the mucosal tissue of left‐sided large bowel cancer cases than that of right‐sided large‐bowel cancer cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ODC activity of the normal mucosa of large bowel may be a useful biomarker of risk for large bowel cancers.

the ODC activity was increased in the normal mucosal tissue in the presence of large bowel cancer, especially in multiple tumors, and that the mucosal activity was higher in left‐sited cases than right‐sided cases.

the ODC activity is higher in the normal mucosal tissues of individuals with multiple tumors and adenoma(s) bearing large bowel adenocarcinomas than in those of the individuals with solitary tumors and without tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mucosal polyamine biosynthase activity may provide a useful biological marker to identify high‐risk groups for the development of large bowel cancer, particularly left‐sided cancers, and thus contribute toward the prevention of mortality.
the polyamine biosynthesis pathway is an excellent target for cancer prevention and treatment.
the ODC activity is a useful marker for the risk of large bowel cancer.
